candidate_strategy.column_contract: 10 columns identical to the prior IRIS manual Path_Traversal projects (aiohttp/airflow/ansible/coderedcms/copyparty): node, role, callableName, flowKind, receiver, moduleHint, argIndex, file, line, matchKind ('ast' vs 'api' rows kept strictly separate)

coverage_gaps: Dynamic dispatch: Tornado handler dispatch is framework-internal (Application(routes)); handler methods are matched by HTTP-verb name + file location, not by resolved route tables - a handler class not named in JSONBlaster.handlers would still match the verb-method family but its URL binding is unknown

sockjs event dispatch is dynamic: getattr(self, event) in _StructuredSocketConnection.on_message (handlers.py:514) - event handlers matched via the @...event decorator, which covers the observed handlers (start/pause/resume/pong)

The blaster blob URI 'blob:<sig>' -> urlparse(parts.path) -> BlobCache[sig] chain crosses a string-split boundary (urlparse) that the later taint config will need as a summary/flow step; recorded here because extraction only marks the endpoints (json_body source, blobcache open/link sinks)

Flask default (string) converter route params cannot contain '/', so '<rootdir>'/'<gididx>' traversal requires the path-converter params; both are emitted with the same flow_kind and the labeling step distinguishes exploitability

Django form-cleaned data -> generate_cookie scopeurls -> scope list -> file: object URI -> open() is a multi-service chain; only the endpoints are extracted (request form sources, object_.py open sinks). No cross-service taint is possible in a single-DB pass; inter-service edges would need MySummaries entries in Phase 2
